changes.after: A package is a collection of R code. Two functions can share a name but come from different places.

before:
library attaches an installed package’s exported names to the search path. Another binding can mask an unqualified name. package::name selects that package’s exported object directly without attaching all of its names; it does not install a missing package.

library(stats) attaches the already installed stats package so its exported median can be found by an unmasked name. This fresh-script example installs nothing; the separate masked-name example below still shows why explicit stats::median can matter.
```r
library(stats)
cat(median(c(1, 9, 5)), "\n", sep = "")
```
It prints:
```text
5
```

stats is included in this R installation. Its median selects the middle ordered value for this odd-length vector. A local function named median can coexist with stats::median. Avoid package:::internal as an application contract: unexported internals may change. Record R and package versions; do not assume an attached package implies the latest release.

Complete local R example; the app itself does not execute it:
```r
median <- function(x) -1
cat(median(c(1, 9, 5)), "\n")
cat(stats::median(c(1, 9, 5)), "\n")
```

Expected output or behavior: -1
5. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.
